Notes on caching HTTP responses

Conditional requests let a client ask a server whether a resource changed since it was last fetched. The client sends the validators it remembers, an entity tag or a modification date, and the server answers with a short status when nothing changed.

This saves bandwidth for both sides, but only works when the client stores the validators between runs. A crawler that forgets them after every run downloads every page in full, even when nothing on the page is new.

The safest approach is to persist the validators together with the content hash, so a changed page can be detected even when a server sends no validators at all.
